title: Frequency Ledger
candidate_instructions: Restate the task and clarify edge cases before proposing an approach.
Explain the data structures and complexity before implementation.
Test with a normal case, an edge case, and one failure-prone case.
interviewer_instructions: Ask what should happen when a count returns to zero.
Ask how first-appearance order can be preserved without sorting.
Observe whether the candidate checks the stated non-negative-count invariant.

title: Bounded Sensor Window
candidate_instructions: Clarify the empty-input and boundary behavior.
Develop the single-pass invariant aloud before coding.
Explain the amortized cost and test repeated extrema.
interviewer_instructions: Ask why rescanning the current window is too expensive.
Ask how expired minimum and maximum values leave the data structure.
Observe whether the candidate can state and preserve a window invariant.

title: Merge Service Queues
candidate_instructions: Clarify stream exhaustion and timestamp ties.
Explain why the memory bound shapes the approach.
Test one empty stream and multiple tied timestamps.
interviewer_instructions: Ask how the candidate enforces deterministic tie-breaking.
Ask for time and auxiliary-space complexity in terms of streams and events.
Observe whether the implementation advances exactly one source per output.

title: Transit Network Reachability
candidate_instructions: Define precisely what counts as a transfer.
Choose graph state that prevents repeated route expansion.
Test same-stop, unreachable, and transfer-boundary cases.
interviewer_instructions: Ask whether routes or stops should be the primary traversal state.
Ask how the maximum-transfer bound changes the search.
Observe whether both visited routes and visited stops are handled deliberately.

title: URL Shortener
candidate_instructions: State functional scope and scale assumptions before drawing components.
Trace the write and redirect paths through the design.
Choose one risk or tradeoff for a deeper discussion.
interviewer_instructions: Ask how short codes are generated and collisions are handled.
Probe cache behavior, abuse controls, and a storage outage.
Keep scale assumptions candidate-owned; there is no hidden official number.

title: Notification Service
candidate_instructions: Clarify channels, delivery semantics, and user preferences.
Separate request acceptance from provider delivery.
Explain retry, idempotency, and observable status.
interviewer_instructions: Probe quiet hours, priorities, and provider-specific failures.
Ask how duplicate delivery is limited across retries.
Observe whether the candidate distinguishes accepted, delivered, and failed.

title: Ticket Reservation System
candidate_instructions: Name the inventory invariant and scope the purchase flow.
Separate browsing, temporary holds, and authoritative reservation.
Discuss contention, expiration, and ambiguous payment outcomes.
interviewer_instructions: Probe how overselling is prevented under concurrency.
Ask what happens when payment succeeds but confirmation times out.
Observe whether hot-event load is isolated from authoritative inventory.

title: Recommendation System
candidate_instructions: Frame the product decision, users, and success metrics first.
Describe a baseline before a more complex model.
Connect training data, serving, and monitoring into one system.
interviewer_instructions: Ask how exposure bias affects labels and evaluation.
Probe retrieval, ranking, policy, and fallback boundaries.
Ask for both quality metrics and product guardrails.

title: Fraud Detection
candidate_instructions: Define the actions and asymmetric costs before choosing metrics.
Address delayed, selective, and adversarial labels.
Explain the online scoring path, fallback, and review capacity.
interviewer_instructions: Ask how score thresholds connect to approve, review, and decline.
Probe delayed chargeback labels and feedback-loop bias.
Ask how the system detects attacker adaptation without leaking policy.

title: RAG Knowledge Assistant
candidate_instructions: Define the user task, evidence boundary, and abstention behavior.
Separate ingestion, retrieval, reranking, context construction, and generation.
Explain permission enforcement and independent retrieval/generation evaluation.
interviewer_instructions: Probe document freshness, deletion, and access-control changes.
Ask how retrieval quality and grounded generation are evaluated separately.
Ask for safe fallbacks when evidence is missing or contradictory.

title: Create Direction Without Authority
candidate_instructions: Choose one truthful example and keep confidential details out.
Keep context concise so personal decisions and actions remain central.
Close with the outcome and what you learned or changed.
interviewer_instructions: Ask what made others trust the direction.
Ask where disagreement was invited and what changed afterward.
Distinguish the candidate's ownership from the group's result.

title: Own a Missed Risk
candidate_instructions: Choose a real risk that was reasonably yours to notice.
Separate immediate recovery from the prevention work that followed.
Explain the durable behavior or system change without deflecting blame.
interviewer_instructions: Ask which signal was available but missed.
Ask what check or behavior exists now because of the experience.
Observe whether accountability is specific and proportionate.

title: Challenge a Technical Direction
candidate_instructions: Describe the disagreement without turning another person into the problem.
Make the evidence, decision process, and your own actions concrete.
Explain the resolution and what the relationship or process learned.
interviewer_instructions: Ask what evidence could have changed the candidate's view.
Ask how the disagreement affected trust and execution.
Observe whether the candidate can explain the other position fairly.
